transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I can’t think straight anymore or make simple decisions at work or school, and it’s starting to scare me. My brain just feels so foggy all the time, and I feel completely overwhelmed trying to keep up.
Did these problems start after a specific stressful event or major life change, or did they come on without a clear trigger? About how long have they been going on most days?

It started about a year ago when I began juggling full-time shifts at the clinic alongside my nursing coursework, which got really overwhelming due to a major staffing shortage. Since then, I've been feeling this way almost every single day, so it's been going on for a little over a year now.

Along with the mental fog and feeling overwhelmed, have you been feeling depressed most of the day or losing interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy? Or does it feel more like constant worry and stress without a persistent low mood?

It's definitely a persistent low mood and a loss of pleasure, not just stress—most days I feel like there's this heavy, gray cloud sitting on my chest and I feel sad and hopeless for no clear reason. I've also completely stopped doing things I used to enjoy, like jogging and knitting, and now I just spend my free time lying in bed scrolling on my phone and ignoring my friends.

Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of harming yourself or ending your life? Also, has this depression made it hard to do basic daily tasks like getting out of bed, showering, eating, or going to work/school?

Yes, on my worst nights when I'm overwhelmed, I catch myself wishing I wouldn't wake up the next morning, which really scares me. It has also completely disrupted my life—I barely eat during my shifts, spend my days off just lying in bed, and I've fallen behind on my coursework and even got written up at the clinic.

When you’re feeling at your lowest, have you ever heard or seen things that other people couldn’t, or felt certain of things like being guilty, ruined, or deserving punishment even when others said it wasn’t true?

No, I’ve never seen or heard things that aren’t there. But I constantly feel consumed by guilt and like I'm completely ruined; whenever I think about my charting error, I spiral into thinking I'm a terrible nurse, a disappointment to my family, and that I deserve to fail because I ruin everything I touch.
Before this past year, have you ever had another separate period lasting at least two weeks when you felt similarly depressed and lost interest in things? If so, did it fully go away in between?

No, I've never gone through anything like this before. This is the first time I've ever felt this way, and it all really started about a year ago when I began juggling my full-time clinic job and my nursing classes.

Have you ever had a period lasting several days or longer when you felt unusually energized or euphoric, needed much less sleep, talked faster than usual, or did risky or impulsive things? Even if it happened before this depression started, please tell me if that has ever happened.
No, I’ve never had any periods where I felt unusually energized, euphoric, or needed much less sleep. I’ve always been more on the anxious or down side, rather than experiencing those kinds of highs.

Are the work and school stressors that started this still ongoing, or did they end and the depression continued anyway? Also, if you had a break from those stressors, did your mood improve much or stay depressed most days?

Yes, the stressors are still very much ongoing because I'm still trying to balance my full-time clinic shifts with my nursing coursework. Even when I have a break on my days off, my mood doesn't improve at all. I just lie in bed feeling sad, empty, and hopeless, unable to shake off that heavy feeling.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a first episode of major depression with persistent depressed mood and marked anhedonia for over a year, accompanied by impaired concentration/indecisiveness, hopelessness, excessive guilt/worthlessness, reduced appetite, psychomotor inactivity/remaining in bed, passive death wishes, and clear occupational/academic impairment. Psychotic symptoms are denied, and there is no history of manic or hypomanic episodes. The severity is supported by suicidal ideation and major functional disruption, consistent with a severe depressive episode without psychotic symptoms.
